intro.text: A people living within Hallandren. Many of them accept the God King as their monarch without counting the Returned as gods.
The original people of the Hallandren lowlands, who once had their own kingdom in the south of the region and now live within Hallandren, many accepting the God King as their monarch.

A small territory under Hallandren's control, absorbed after its defeat in the Manywar. Its people form a separate, easily overlooked community with their own religion, and three centuries on many still long for independence.

description.text: The Pahn Kahl follow a religion of their own. Outsiders often think it simple next to the elaborate doctrine of the Iridescent Tones, and plenty of people, in Hallandren and elsewhere, have no idea it exists.
A sweet pastry called the tinkfan is prized as a delicacy. It is eaten in small bites, with a morsel of bread between each to clear the palate.

Many toil in the dye fields under harsh Hallandren overseers. Some find better but shaky work as Court servants: they must wear brown, may not touch or speak to the God King, cannot serve him though they may serve his wife, are barred from the priesthood, and lose their posts whenever a new God King comes to the throne.

They differ from other Hallandren in skin tone and features and are shorter on average, yet outsiders often fail to tell them apart, to their irritation. Hallandren tends to treat them as second-class and less trustworthy, which rankles a people who lived here first and were conquered by newcomers.

items.text: In early times the Pahn Kahl lived in fishing villages along the coast of the jungle valley. Ships from Chedesh, exploring the coasts, found the region; when one explorer, Vo, died aboard ship in the bay and became the first Returned, his crewmates ignored the natives and founded the kingdom of Hanald there.
As Hanald grew, the Pahn Kahl formed a kingdom of their own, claiming the southern part of the lowlands.
Hanald kept the dye trade to itself, and neighbouring kingdoms, Pahn Kahl among them, came to resent it and hoped to seize a share of the profits.

The Pahn Kahl generally blame the Manywar on Hanald's royal family, who they say chased new Awakening methods and Lifeless without seeing how these could be turned on them. A coalition called the Pahn Unity fought Hanald's forces, and its leader fell at the famous Battle of Twilight Falls.

Under Hallandren the Pahn Kahl came to be seen as second-class, and few outsiders could tell them from their rulers. Though many still wished for independence, the province earned a name for being quiet and peaceful.
Around 321, Vahr, one of the Pahn Kahl, began stirring up dye workers and other dissidents, persuading many to hand him their Breath while he gathered an army. His revolt failed.
Having no army of his own, the God King's steward Bluefingers schemed to set Hallandren and Idris at war, hoping Pahn Kahl could break free amid the fighting.

With Lifeless, hired mercenaries and Pahn Kahl scribes posing as priests, he took the God King's palace and captured the God King and his queen. He won control of the rest of Hallandren's Lifeless by forcing Lightsong and Blushweaver to reveal their Commands, and the army was ordered to march on Idris.
He planned to kill the two gods and leave their bodies among dead Idrians, as though Idrian rebels had struck back, and to kill the royal couple in a way that would also put the blame on Idris.

The plan failed when Lightsong used his divine Breath to heal the God King's maimed tongue, letting Susebron use his immense store of Breath to rescue Siri and defeat the rebels. Vasher then gave Susebron command of Kalad's Phantoms.
